thread:
jin: Heads-up: telemetry is showing inconsistent kernel picks on H100 for short-to-mid seqs (roughly 96-160). Some requests choose gemm_fused, others attention_lin. When it flips we see ~1.8x tail latency for the same model + batch size.

anna: Ugh, that's the region we tuned last month. Do you have raw telemetry examples we can inspect? Preferably the kernel_reason and minimal perf fields (no prompt content).

jin: Pasted a redacted sample from the agent-side telemetry (sampling 0.1%):
```
{HOST: "srv-12", arch: "h100", model: "rwd-3b", seq_len: 128, batch: 1, kernel_chosen: "gemm_fused", kernel_variant: "v2", kernel_reason: "heuristic_short_seq", latency_ms: 2.2, kv_cache_hit: true, quantized: false}
{HOST: "srv-19", arch: "h100", model: "rwd-3b", seq_len: 128, batch: 1, kernel_chosen: "attention_lin", kernel_variant: "opt_small", kernel_reason: "heuristic_seq_bins", latency_ms: 3.9, kv_cache_hit: true, quantized: false}
{HOST: "srv-12", arch: "h100", model: "rwd-3b", seq_len: 160, batch: 1, kernel_chosen: "attention_lin", kernel_variant: "opt_small", kernel_reason: "seq_len>150_path", latency_ms: 2.8}
```
(The actual payload strips prompt/token payloads; these are just routing + perf fields.)

mike: Quick hypotheses:
- The autotuner uses per-arch profiles but we may have stale H100 profiles that expect different micro-batch behaviour.
- The heuristics that pick between gemm_fused vs attention_lin are seq-bin heavy; small changes in seq_len/placeholders can push different thresholds.
- KV cache state may change the effective compute pattern — e.g., cache hits convert to shorter profiler paths.
- Quantization/packed-int paths sometimes cause us to prefer a fallback kernel on some servers.

anna: Can you repro locally with the same driver + CUDA version? Also we need to ensure telemetry reasons are canonicalized (not free text). Right now I see both "heuristic_short_seq" and "heuristic_seq_bins" which complicates aggregation.

jin: Agreed. Proposed immediate changes:
1) Add a structured reason_code enum in telemetry with these values: [arch_pref, profile_match, heuristic_bin, kv_cache_effect, quant_fallback, fallback_nonopt, operator_unavailable].
2) Add an optional decision_trace field for debug sampling that lists the ordered candidates and their score (only for private debug dumps, not production full sampling).
3) Expose debug env flags on the agent for canary: REDWOOD_KERNEL_TELEMETRY=1, REDWOOD_KERNEL_TRACE=decision, REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLING=0.005
4) Server-side: ensure sampling cap and PII-stripper; canonicalize host -> host_pool id instead of full hostname.

mike: For the autotuner, let's also persist per-arch, per-driver microbenchmarks and a last-updated timestamp. If a node's driver mismatch > X weeks, mark profile stale and force deterministic kernel picks.

anna: Privacy/security note: ensure decision_trace never includes prompt tokens. Also we should add an opt-out env for customers: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_KERNEL_REASONS=0.

jin: I'll create a small patch that
- introduces reason_code enum
- wires REDWOOD_KERNEL_TELEMETRY and REDWOOD_KERNEL_TRACE envs
- adds a canary config to sample decision_trace at 0.1% and telemetry header-only at 0.5%

deploy-bot: canary rollout started: kernel-telemetry-v2 -> 10% of h100 pool (tag: canary-kbelt-2026.03.17)

anna: Nice. Post-deploy checks:
- aggregation dashboard with counts by reason_code and median latency by (reason_code, seq_bin, arch)
- alert if median latency for any reason_code exceeds baseline by 25% for 30m
- inspect host_pool variance; if variance high, revert canary.

jin: I'll open a PR and attach a raw-sample export (sanitized). Also creating a small perf test to hit seq_len=96..160 many times to force boundary transitions.

mike: One more: let's add kernel_selection_hash in telemetry so we can correlate exact decision inputs across hosts.

jin: Sounds good. I'll iterate on the patch today and ping @anna and @mike for review. Thanks.
